summary: Generated an action-complete teacher corpus from the legal receding-horizon planner with every legal sibling labelled under common random numbers, trained a student against within-root ranking losses, and reported a failed offline gate without opening a gameplay cohort; separately found that the eight-tape cohort underlying the teacher's reported advantage was unrepresentative.
validationPerformed: Information-boundary, frozen-planner-equivalence, sibling-completeness, afterstate-reality and half-averaging gates all passed; ranking and play parity 120 moves, 0 mismatches; exported-versus-PyTorch agreement to 8.6e-6.
Action completeness 1.0000 over 108,462 labelled siblings with zero missing and zero illegal labels.
limitations: Recorded by the coordinator on the delegated agent's behalf; the agent had no write access to research/ and did not review this transcription.
Exploratory namespace only; does not upgrade docs/research/ or any frozen protocol.
Offline gate failed, so no gameplay cohort was opened and the shared evaluation cohort remains untouched for this candidate.
The teacher ran at a reduced horizon relative to the configuration whose strength was originally reported, so teacher weakening and cohort size are partially confounded.
The epsilon-exploration cohort was dropped under machine contention, so the corpus is entirely on-policy and distribution shift is untested.
